The register says applicant: "Keli Electric Manufacturing (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."
The document says: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."

These are genuinely different company names — "Keli Electric Manufacturing" vs "Keli Sensing Technology". These are not spelling drift or legal suffix drift; the core entity names differ. Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. is a real company that makes load cells (relevant to R60, which is the OIML recommendation for weighing load cells). "Keli Electric Manufacturing" appears to be a register entry error or a different company. Actually, Keli Sensing Technology is well-known for load cells. So this is a genuinely different company name → different-entity, best_value = the document's.

The rule: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Keli Sensing Technology (Ningbo) Co., Ltd."
